summary: Implemented patch::write_chart_edits for borrowed Write + ?Sized sinks, sharing planning, full preflight validation, and byte chunk traversal with the existing buffered API. Added WritePatchError with typed error sources and eight integration tests.

design_decisions: Both public output paths invoke the same Planner and ValidatedSplices preflight. All planned ranges are bounds-checked before sorting, then overlaps are checked before any writer method is called. The existing (start, end, seq) sort order is unchanged.

A shared iterator borrows unchanged input slices and owned planner fragments. The streaming API never invokes the buffered output method or clones the input/output XML; existing structural fragment allocation remains permitted.

The new API borrows &mut W with W: Write + ?Sized, supporting trait objects and leaving writer ownership, flushing, and closing to the caller. write_all supplies short-write, Interrupted, and WriteZero behavior.

WritePatchError keeps PatchError and io::Error as separate public variants. Both implement Error; source returns the original typed cause, and the I/O error is moved unchanged, retaining its custom payload. I/O failures stop immediately and can leave a prefix; validation failures perform no writer calls.
Existing public function signatures, structs, enums, and variants remain intact. Added Error for PatchError instead of changing its representation. Existing inline tests were preserved.
Checked clone-template slicing and replaced debug-only width assertions with explicit errors so malformed clone coordinates and empty clone templates fail before output instead of panicking.

Integration tests exercise every ChartEdit variant, mixed structural/value edits, coincident append ordering, exact preservation of unedited bytes, trait-object sinks, late planning/bounds/overlap failures, malformed clone coordinates, short writes, interruption retries, WriteZero, custom error payload identity, and no flushing.
limitations: This is an isolated crate implementation and test run, not an upstream contribution, full document-engine integration, or visual validation.
No allocation benchmark or peak-memory metric was collected. The absence of complete-output buffering on the streaming path was established by its implementation structure.
The caller must continue to supply ChartData scanned from the same XML. I/O failures cannot roll back bytes accepted by the caller-owned sink.
